LESSON: SUBTRACTION

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four
Subject: MATHEMATICS FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.3: SUBTRACTION
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers SUBTRACTION, part of Strand 1 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four MATHEMATICS FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: Why do you use subtraction in real life? 2. How do you create patterns involving subtraction?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. sign terms related to subtraction,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of SUBTRACTION in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. subtract up to 4-digit numbers with regrouping in real life situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of SUBTRACTION in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. estimate difference by rounding off numbers to the nearest ten in real life situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of SUBTRACTION in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. create patterns involving subtraction from up to 10,000,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of SUBTRACTION in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. use digital devices for learning subtractions,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of SUBTRACTION in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

F. appreciate application of subtraction of numbers in real life situations. ● In pairs or groups, learners are to be guided to fingerspell, sign and subtract and present numbers up to 4-digit numbers without regrouping in real life situations. ● In groups, learners in class are to be guided to watch captioned or signed videos on subtraction of numbers up to 4 digits and write down the steps. ● In pairs or groups or individually learners are to be guided to subtract up to 4- digit numbers with 1. Why do you use subtraction in real life? 2. How do you create patterns involving subtraction? 13 regrouping using number cards. ● In pairs or groups, learners are guided to estimate and work out the difference by rounding off the numbers to the nearest ten in real life situations. ● In pairs or groups, learners are guided to discuss, create and display patterns involving subtraction of numbers from up to 10,000. ● In pairs or groups, learners are guided to play games involving subtraction using digital devices or other resources available, then work out the 14 exercises given in the text.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on SUBTRACTION together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Creativity and imagination: use creativity in work contexts as they create patterns involving subtraction of numbers

from up to 10,000.

● Digital literacy: play digital games as learners- in pairs or groups play games involving subtraction using digital

devices or other resources.

Values:
• Respect: enhanced as learners in groups discuss subtraction of numbers up to 4-digit numbers without regrouping using

number cards.

• Responsibility: cares for own property and that of others as learners work in groups using digital devices and other

learning materials.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Life skills and human population: problem solving as learners apply subtraction of numbers in real life situations.

Link to other learning areas:

Learners relate display of patterns in pairs or groups as they discuss, create and display patterns involving subtraction of

numbers from up to 10,000 to creation of patterns in Creative Arts.

Suggested Resources:

Place value chart, Abacus, relevant digital devices, relevant digital devices etc.
